originalTitle: Raymond Realty Q1 net profit falls 19 pc to Rs 13.43 cr on higher expenses
simplifiedContent: Raymond Realty, a company, made less profit (19% less) in the first quarter of the year because it spent more on expenses. Even with higher expenses, the company still made more money overall, with total income reaching Rs 535.71 crore. The company also had a good quarter in terms of selling properties, with sales bookings of Rs 700 crore, which is a big increase from last year. This means that despite higher costs, the company is still selling a lot of properties and making more money overall. This is important because it shows how the company is performing financially, which can affect its stock price.

originalTitle: Gold hits seven-week high as weak U.S. jobs data dents rate hike bets
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has gone up to its highest point in seven weeks. This happened because the US recently reported a loss of jobs, which was unexpected. As a result, people think it's less likely that interest rates will be raised soon, making gold a more attractive investment. This is also helping the prices of other precious metals like silver and platinum to rise. Overall, gold is having its best week in seven months, which is good news for people who have invested in it.

originalTitle: Airbnb shares surge 15% to four-year high on raised forecast, AI gains
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: Airbnb's stock price jumped up by 15% to its highest point in four years. This happened because the company said it expects to make more money this year than it previously thought, due to people still wanting to travel and the company using artificial intelligence to work more efficiently. The company also made more money than expected in the last quarter and spent less on customer support, which made investors happy. This is important because it shows that investors are confident in Airbnb's ability to succeed, even with some uncertainty in the world, like tensions in the Middle East. Overall, it's a positive sign for the company and its investors.

originalTitle: Sebi to cut routine checks by two-thirds, focus on high-risk players
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is changing the way it monitors the stock market. It plans to reduce the number of regular checks it does by about two-thirds. This means SEBI will be inspecting fewer companies and focusing more on those that are considered high-risk. This change is intended to make SEBI's process more efficient. By focusing on high-risk players, SEBI aims to better protect investors and the market.

originalTitle: Weekly Winner: Ujaas Energy jumps 68% this week as upbeat Q1 earnings fuel buying
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: Ujaas Energy's stock price went up by 68% this week, which is a big jump. This happened because the company just released its quarterly earnings report, which showed that it made more money than it did last year. Specifically, its net profit increased by 31% compared to the same time last year, and this is because it sold more solar power systems. This good news made investors want to buy more of the company's stock, which drove up the price to ₹257.80. This matters because it could be a sign that the company is doing well and may continue to grow.

originalTitle: Cupid net profit jumps 194% YoY to  ₹44 crore in Q1 as margins expand sharply; raises FY27 guidance
simplifiedContent: Cupid, a company, made a lot more money in the first quarter of the year compared to the same time last year. Its net profit, which is the amount of money it has left after paying all its expenses, increased by 194% to ₹44 crore. The company's revenue, which is the total amount of money it earned, also went up by 142% to ₹157 crore. This growth was mainly due to its healthcare business doing well both in India and other countries. The company is now expecting to do even better for the whole year, which is why it has raised its guidance for the year.
